papers.title: Plane wave representation for wave scattering on a sphere
papers.abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.

papers.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
papers.abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.

papers.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of K\"ahler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform \`a priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.

papers.title: Oka realizations, fundamental groups, and holomorphic cofibrations
papers.abstract: The homotopy types of Oka manifolds are exactly those of countable finite-dimensional CW complexes. We construct realizations as open subsets of complex Euclidean spaces with explicit dimension bounds. Other realizations have good open covers by sets biholomorphic to $\C^N$, with prescribed finite nerves, or are unions of Fatou--Bieberbach domains whose nonempty finite intersections are again Fatou--Bieberbach domains. Every nonempty Stein manifold admits a proper holomorphic embedding into an Oka open subset of some $\C^N$, and this embedding is a homotopy equivalence. We obtain holomorphic representatives of ordinary and generalized cohomology classes, and realize every countable group as the fundamental group of an Oka domain in $\C^5$. The fundamental groups of algebraically elliptic manifolds are precisely the finite groups, and every virtually abelian K\"ahler group is the fundamental group of a projective Oka manifold. Finally, we classify holomorphic cofibrations in L\'arusson's intermediate model structures and establish factorizations over aspherical targets into proper holomorphic embeddings and holomorphic fibre bundles with Oka fibre.

papers.title: On the k-th Milnor and k-th Tjurina Numbers of a Foliation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notions of the $k$-th Milnor number and the $k$-th Tjurina number for a germ of holomorphic foliation on the complex plane with an isolated singularity at the origin. We develop a detailed study of these invariants, establishing explicit formulas and relating them to other indices associated with holomorphic foliations. In particular, we obtain an explicit expression for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation and, as a consequence, a formula for the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function. We analyze their topological behavior, proving that the $k$-th Milnor number of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant, whereas the $k$-th Tjurina number is not. In dimension two, we provide a positive answer to a conjecture posed by Hussain, Liu, Yau, and Zuo concerning a sharp lower bound for the $k$-th Tjurina number of a weighted homogeneous polynomial. We also present a counterexample to another conjecture of Hussain, Yau, and Zuo regarding the ratio between these invariants. Moreover, we establish a fundamental relation linking the $k$-th Tjurina numbers of a foliation and of an invariant curve via the G\'omez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index, and we extend Teissier's Lemma to the setting of $k$-th polar intersection numbers. In addition, we derive an upper bound for the $k$-th Milnor number of a foliation in terms of its $k$-th Tjurina number along balanced divisors of separatrices. Finally, for non-dicritical quasi-homogeneous foliations, we obtain a closed formula for their $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers.

papers.title: Bounded Toeplitz operators and unbounded projected multiplication
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth, nonnegative radial symbol $g$ on $\mathbb C$ whose Toeplitz operator on Bargmann--Fock space is positive with singular values decaying faster than every exponential, while projected multiplication $f\mapsto P(gf)$ has no bounded extension from the ambient Gaussian $L^2$ space. All heat transforms of $g$ at positive times are Schwartz functions, and $g\in L^p(dA)$ for every $0<p<2$. We also construct smooth real symbols realizing every possible set of heat boundedness times. Any prescribed positive threshold may be included or excluded, with Schwartz transforms at every later time. All these symbols satisfy the coherent state domain condition, and all heat integrals converge absolutely.

papers.title: Wave scattering by a transversal defect in a discrete waveguide
papers.abstract: We study wave scattering by a finite transversal strip in a discrete square-lattice waveguide with Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on the strip and the waveguide walls. The setting is motivated as a discrete analogue of the classical continuous waveguide problem with a screen. The corresponding Wiener--Hopf formulation leads to an equation with a $4 \times 4$ matrix kernel, which reduces to a $2 \times 2$ matrix kernel under some symmetry assumptions. The prospects for factorising this kernel are discussed, but this approach is not pursued. Instead, an exact analytical solution is obtained using the pole removal technique. This contrasts with the continuous case, where only approximate solutions are currently available. The reflection and transmission coefficients resulting from an incident duct mode are computed with an accuracy up to $10^{-13}$, showing consistency with theoretical predictions from continuous waveguide theory. In particular, full reflection and zero transmission are recovered as the frequency approaches the cut-off value for the incident mode. Finally, the solution is validated against a numerical computation of the diffraction problem via the Boundary Algebraic Equations method with a tailored lattice Green's function.

papers.title: Sharp degree bound for rational proper maps from $\mathbb B^2$ to $\mathbb B^4$
papers.abstract: We prove that every rational proper holomorphic map from $\mathbb{B}^2$ to $\mathbb{B}^4$ has degree at most $5$, confirming D'Angelo's conjecture in this case. This sharp bound follows from Meylan's degree estimates and an intersection-theoretic argument ruling out degree $6$.

papers.title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $\tau\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_\tau g(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \tau_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $\tau\mapsto T_\tau$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_\tau$ to the inverse of $\tau$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $\tau$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $\tau$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.

papers.title: Characterizations for quasiconformal weighted Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of planar quasiconformal mappings in weighted Bergman spaces $A_\alpha^p(\mathbb D)$. For $p>0$ and $\alpha>-1$, our characterization involves the convergence of certain integrals involving superlevel set areas, the Hausdorff measure of boundary superlevel sets, and the averaged derivative. These include quasiconformal analogues of characterizations established by Karafyllia and Karamanlis for conformal mappings. Moreover, for $-1<\alpha\leq 0$, we obtain an additional equivalent characterization in terms of the Hausdorff measure of level sets. The power $\alpha$ is sharp: for every $\alpha>0$, we construct a bounded $K_\alpha$-quasiconformal mapping for which the weighted level-set length integral with exponent $\alpha+2$ diverges.

papers.title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
papers.abstract: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $\deg p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=\alpha\,q(\beta z+h)+k$ or $p(z)=\alpha\,\bar q(\beta z+h)+k$ for some $\alpha,\beta,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.

papers.title: Absolute moments of GH distribution
papers.abstract: In this work, we focus on deriving the absolute moments of the general ized hyperbolic (GH) distribution via its mean-variance mixture structure. Conditioning on the GIG mixing variable reduces the problem to Gaussian moment calculations and known GIG power moments, avoiding direct integration with Bessel functions. The variance gamma (VG), normal inverse Gaussian (NIG), hyperbolic, Normal, and Student t distributions emerge as natural special or limiting cases of the generalized hyperbolic family. This approach offers a substantially simpler and more transparent derivation, facilitating both implementation and verification.

papers.title: Averaged derivatives and reverse inequalities in quasiregular Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We study weighted Bergman spaces of quasiregular mappings on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with weight $(1-|x|)^\alpha$, $\alpha>-1$. For every fixed distortion bound $K\ge1$ and every $p>0$, we characterize Bergman integrability by averaged derivatives. We also give geometric conditions under which integration over a subset, or against another measure, controls the full Bergman integral. When $K$ is sufficiently large, the dominating sets are precisely the relatively dense sets. For comparison, we determine the dominating sets for the M\"obius class $K=1$ in dimensions $n\ge3$. At the critical exponent $p=n+\alpha$, its domination criterion differs from that for every fixed $K>1$. Our results extend aspects of the Bergman theory developed by Nolder~\cite{Nolder90} and by Oleinik and Vuorinen~\cite{OV}, and complement the recent work of Adamowicz and Gonz\'alez~\cite{AG21,AG25} and Adamowicz and Caama\~no~\cite{AC} on quasiregular Hardy spaces.

papers.title: Uniform Green packing on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on Laplace designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with the help of ChatGPT.

papers.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.

papers.title: A counterexample concerning the coefficient formula for de Branges-Rovnyak norms
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}(b)$ be the de Branges-Rovnyak space associated to a non-extreme point $b$ of the unit ball of $H^\infty$, and let $\phi=b/a$, where $a$ is the Pythagorean mate of $b$. In an earlier article, the author showed that, if $\phi\in H^2$, then \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b) \iff \Bigl(f\in H^2 \text{ and }\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr), \] in which case we have \[ \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}(b)}^2=\sum_{m\ge0}|\hat{f}(m)|^2 +\sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2. \] It was also shown that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $\phi\in\cap_{p<2}H^p$, yet \[ f\in\mathcal{H}(b)\not\Rightarrow \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty. \] Here we complete this circle of ideas by showing that there exists a space $\mathcal{H}(b)$ for which $\phi\in\cap_{p<1}H^p$, yet \[ \Bigl(f\in H^2\text{ and } \sum_{m\ge0}\Bigl|\sum_{n\ge0}\overline{\hat{\phi}(n)}\hat{f}(m+n)\Bigr|^2<\infty\Bigr) \not\Rightarrow f\in\mathcal{H}(b). \]

papers.title: Maximum-modulus points on concentric circles
papers.abstract:
Let $f$ be a nonzero, non-monomial entire function, and let $
u_f(r)$ count the points at which $f$ attains its maximum modulus on $|z|=r$. Write $f(z)=z^m(a_0+a_kz^k+O(z^{k+1}))$, where $a_0a_k
e0$. We prove that $
u_f(r)\le 2k$ outside a locally finite subset of $(0,\infty)$. The constant $2k$ is sharp. In particular, $\liminf_{r	o\infty}
u_f(r)<\infty$, so the number of maximum-modulus points of a fixed non-monomial entire function cannot tend to infinity on all sufficiently large circles. The proof associates the logarithmic derivative $q=zf'/f$ with its reflection $q^*(w)=\overline{q( ar w)}$ through the correspondence $q(z)=q^*(w)$ and the map $(z,w)\mapsto(zw,q(z))$. Local valence at the origin bounds the number of inverse pairs that can escape. A local elimination argument then bounds the generic degree of each nonvertical image component. The residue structure of $f'/f$ excludes vertical components.

papers.title: Sparsity and uniformity in dynamical Manin--Mumford problems
papers.abstract: For endomorphisms of the complex projective plane of a given degree, we prove that the existence of a special curve of bounded degree, in the sense of the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture, is confined to a proper algebraic subvariety of the parameter space. This confirms a conjecture of DeMarco and Mavraki in dimension two. For general regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb A^k$, we obtain a uniform dynamical Manin--Mumford bound outside an exceptional hypersurface. These results arise from a common strategy, valid in every dimension and codimension, which reduces such questions to the geometry of exceptional loci in the space of pairs formed by subvarieties and maps. We control these loci by combining arithmetic equidistribution, blender constructions, dynamical directions, monodromy arguments, and degenerations at the boundary of parameter space.

papers.title: A computer-assisted proof of Krzy\.z's conjecture for the sixth coefficient
papers.abstract: We prove Krzy\.z's conjecture for the sixth coefficient. Every holomorphic function $f(z)=\sum a_kz^k$ from the unit disk to the punctured disk satisfies $|a_6| \le 2/e$. Equality holds precisely for rotations of $\exp(-(1-z^6)/(1+z^6))$. Every extremal has a Herglotz representation with at most six atoms. By the reduction of Agler and McCarthy and the entropy theorem of Lei and Zhang, it suffices to exclude extremals with fewer than six atoms. We do this by a rigorous computer-assisted branch-and-bound, leaving the equality case entirely to the analytic argument. The main ingredients are explicit first-order conditions for extremals with fewer than the maximal number of atoms, which reduce to Chebyshev relations when one atom is missing, and a bound for the total mass obtained by convexity of the Poisson integral. The same method independently establishes the full-degree property for the known cases $n=3,4,5$.

papers.title: Quaternionic Elasticity Theory with Local Fractional Derivatives
papers.abstract: We develop a quaternionic formulation of linear elasticity in which the classical derivative is replaced by Yang's local fractional derivative and the classical Cauchy--Riemann operator by a fractal Cauchy--Riemann operator. We formulate fractal kinematics, a constitutive law with a material length scale and the equilibrium equation, and show that, for displacement fields with polynomial components, the resulting homogeneous fractal Lam\'e system is equivalent to the monogenicity of an explicit quaternionic field. On the polynomial sector, that is, for finite combinations of normalized fractal monomials, we prove a fractal Kolosov--Muskhelishvili representation of the displacement field in terms of two monogenic quaternionic potentials, together with its completeness, by a direct construction that uses neither the Galerkin nor the Papkovich--Neuber potentials. The position term of the classical formula has to be replaced by a corrected position operator, which satisfies the exact Weyl relation with the partial local fractional derivatives. Finally a fractal Papkovich-Neuber representation is derived.

papers.title: The sharp constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality
papers.abstract: We prove that the optimal constant in the Chang--Marshall inequality is $e$, as conjectured by Andreev and Matheson. More precisely, if $f$ is analytic in the unit disk, vanishes to order $m\geq1$ at the origin, and has normalized Dirichlet integral $d\leq1$, then the boundary mean of $e^{|f|^2}$ is at most $e^{d/m}$. Equality holds precisely for monomials. The proof uses an auxiliary closed planar curve and the isoperimetric inequality to establish monotonicity of the exponential functional along normalized radial dilations.

papers.title: Oka complements in algebraic tori and their logarithmic covers
papers.abstract: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $K\subset\C^n$ is compact and polynomially convex. Write $q(z)=(e^{-iz_1},\ldots,e^{-iz_n})$, $X_K=(\C^*)^n\setminus(K\cap(\C^*)^n)$, and $Y_K=\C^n\setminus q^{-1}(K)$. We prove that $X_K$ and its logarithmic covering $Y_K$ are Oka. More strongly, $Y_K$ admits normalized holomorphic families of entire embeddings through prescribed holomorphic sections. The proof combines polynomial pair Hamiltonian transport in multiplicative coordinates, compatible with the coordinate hyperplanes, with a fixed Fatou--Bieberbach model. Applications include Oka slab crosses over arbitrary nonempty connected planar domains, complements of periodic equal-radius Euclidean balls centered at products of planar lattices, and complements of sufficiently small closed metric balls in products of elliptic curves.

papers.title: Toeplitz determinants for starlike mappings of order {\alpha} in several complex variables
papers.abstract: Let $F(z)=zf(z)$, where $f$ is a normalized scalar holomorphic function on the unit ball $\mathbb B$ of a complex Banach space $X$ or on the unit polydisk $\mathbb U^n$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$. We establish sharp bounds for two Toeplitz determinants involving the second, third and fourth Fr\'echet derivatives of $F$ when $F$ is starlike of order $\alpha$, $0\leq\alpha<1$. The first bound is sharp for the full range $0\leq\alpha<1$, while the second is sharp for $0\leq\alpha\leq 2/3$. The extremal mappings are explicitly identified, confirming the sharpness of the estimates.

papers.title: On Mok's uniqueness problem of holomorphic isometries from complex unit balls of maximal dimension into classical domains
papers.abstract: We prove that every holomorphic isometric embedding, with respect to the Bergman metrics, from a complex unit ball of maximal dimension into irreducible classical bounded symmetric domain of rank at least two that is not biholomorphic to a Type IV domain is equivalent to Mok's embedding. This completely resolves a problem of Mok.

papers.title: Contractivity of Rudin's diagonal restriction operator for $H^p$ of the polydisc
papers.abstract: We establish that Rudin's diagonal restriction operator is contractive from the Hardy space $H^p$ of the bidisc to the Bergman space $A^p$ of the disc for $2\leq p<\infty$, and characterize all cases of equality. We extend the result to polydiscs and obtain applications to polynomial point evaluation among others. The proof relies on an explicit formula, deduced from certain Green's formulas, for the defect between the $p$th powers of the two $L^p$ norms.

papers.title: The Fekete-Szeg\"{o} problem for starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ and quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit balls of complex Banach spaces
papers.abstract: We establish sharp estimates for the generalized Zalcman functional corresponding to the index $n=2$ for normalized starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ and normalized quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit ball of a complex Banach space and on the unit polydisk in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We also derive sharp Fekete-Szeg\"{o} inequalities for normalized starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ and normalized quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ in the unit ball of a complex Banach space. Our results extend classical coefficient estimates to higher-dimensional holomorphic mappings and provide a partial confirmation of the generalized Zalcman conjecture in higher dimensions.

papers.title: Fatou Components of Attracting Skew Products: From Polynomial Classification to Transcendental Complexity
papers.abstract: We study the Fatou components of holomorphic skew products $F \colon \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2, F(z,w) = (f(z) + r(z,w), g(w))$ near an attracting invariant fiber, introducing a refined classification of components on the fiber: bulging, partial bulging, and nowhere bulging. For polynomial skew products, we give a complete characterization of when the basin at infinity is non-bulging, and show that in this case non-bulging implies nowhere bulging, ruling out partial bulging entirely. In the transcendental setting, the behavior is richer: we construct partially bulging wandering domains and Baker domains, show that any orbitally unbounded Fatou component can be made nowhere bulging by choosing an appropriate function $r$, and prove that for any nonconstant $r$ there exists an entire function $f$ with an escaping wandering domain that fails to be bulging. Bulging thus depends on the interplay between fiber dynamics and perturbation.

papers.title: Interpolation by Rational $\Gamma_{E(3; 3; 1, 1, 1)}$-Inner Function and Rational $\Gamma_{E(3; 2; 1, 2)}$-Inner Function
papers.abstract: We study several function-theoretic aspects of the domains $G_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$ and $G_{E(3;2;1,2)}$. We introduce and investigate the notions of $\Gamma_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$-inner functions and $\Gamma_{E(3;2;1,2)}$-inner functions, and establish their relationships with $\Gamma_{E(2;2;1,1)}$-inner functions and $\Gamma_{E(2;1;2)}$-inner functions. We provide explicit constructions and representations of rational $\Gamma_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$-inner functions and rational $\Gamma_{E(3;2;1,2)}$-inner functions. As an application of these results, we obtain partial solutions to the associated interpolation problems and construct explicit rational inner interpolants for interpolation data lying in suitable subsets of $G_{E(3;3;1,1,1)}$ and $G_{E(3;2;1,2)}$, respectively.

papers.title: The Bloch constant is strictly smaller than the Ahlfors--Grunsky value
papers.abstract: We prove that the classical Bloch constant is strictly smaller than the Ahlfors--Grunsky value, disproving the famous Bloch constant conjecture. The Lean 4 formalization of the main results are also provided.

papers.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.
